questions.q: Which sentence evaluates rather than reports?
options: Text A says uniforms save families money.
Text B thinks uniforms are uncomfortable.
Text A's claim that uniforms save money rests on one shop's prices, so the evidence is weak.
questions.why: Evaluation judges how convincing an idea is, e.g. by testing its evidence.

questions.q: What register suits a directed writing letter to your headteacher?
options: Chatty, with slang to sound friendly
questions.why: Register must match the audience: a headteacher needs a formal, respectful letter.

questions.q: A student summarises Text A, then Text B, with no judgement. What is the likely result?
options: Full reading marks if every idea is included
No effect if the summary is accurate
The reading mark is capped in the middle levels
questions.why: Top reading marks need evaluation of both texts, not just reporting.

questions.q: Give two questions you could ask to evaluate an idea in one of the texts.
questions.model: Any two: What evidence supports it, and is it enough? Could the writer be biased? Is it exaggerated or one-sided? Does it apply to everyone? Does the other text support or contradict it?
points: bias, exaggeration, limits, or comparison with the other text
